components.title: Site sign-in
components.description: Keycloak for passkey sign-in, with its realm applier and its Postgres database.

control-implementations.description: What the realm as code, the rendered Keycloak release and the site's signed evidence export show about sign-in.

implemented-requirements.description: People sign in to the site with a passkey or security key only.

statements.description: The realm as code (deploy/keycloak/realm.json), prepared with the CI site file at both signInKeys levels, has no password, one-time-code or recovery-code step in any authentication flow, binds every flow slot to a flow it defines, lets no client use direct grants, and keeps the update-password, one-time-code and recovery-code required actions off with passwordless registration on; the realm check refuses a copy that breaks any of these before anything is applied. On the running site, the signed evidence export counts no enabled password and no one-time-code authenticator in the flows the live realm binds.
statements.remarks: Your organization applies the reviewed realm as code to the site's Keycloak, enrols each person's passkey or security key, and produces the site's evidence export at least weekly.

implemented-requirements.description: The site setting signInKeys sets how strong a sign-in key must be.

statements.description: At both signInKeys levels the realm's passwordless policy requires user verification and a resident key and refuses a second registration of the same authenticator, and its relying-party ID is the one value the site file names; an empty value or one that is not a bare domain name is refused before the realm is applied. Under passkeys the realm asks for no attestation and keeps no allowlist of authenticator models, so a synced phone passkey is accepted. Under hardware-only it asks for direct or enterprise attestation, accepts only the authenticator models (AAGUIDs) on the site's allowlist, and needs the site's attestation roots; the realm check refuses an empty allowlist, attestation none, or an allowlist under passkeys.
statements.remarks: Your organization chooses each site's level and its allowlist of authenticator models; hardware-only is the recommended setting for defence production. Cross-device (hybrid QR) passkey sign-in needs an Apple or Google internet relay, so it is unavailable at an air-gapped site. Your organization also sets the relying-party ID to its one shared parent domain.

implemented-requirements.description: Signing with a person's long-term key needs a fresh sign-in.

statements.description: The realm as code defines a second authentication level that is reached only by a fresh WebAuthn ceremony and stays valid only for the site's step-up window, read from the site file; both signInKeys levels have the same step-up flows. The confidential session client puts its own audience, acr and auth_time in the access token, so the services behind it can check how recently and how the person signed in. The realm check refuses a longer level-2 window, a missing audience or a token without auth_time.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the step-up window in the site file.

implemented-requirements.description: Keycloak records sign-in and administration events.

statements.description: The realm as code turns on login events and admin events with their details, written through the jboss-logging listener, and Keycloak renders with JSON console logs; the realm check refuses a realm with admin events off. On the running site, the signed evidence export reports user and admin events on and counts the realm's events that reached the site log store in the last day.
statements.remarks: Your organization reviews the site's sign-in and administration events.

implemented-requirements.description: Only administrators create and change accounts.

statements.description: The realm as code allows no self-registration, no password reset and no username change, keeps emails unique, and lets only administrators change a person's email; the realm check refuses a realm that allows duplicate emails or lets a person edit their own email.
statements.remarks: Your organization's administrators create, enrol, change and remove people's accounts.

implemented-requirements.description: Keycloak reaches its database over verified TLS.

statements.description: Keycloak, rendered from the locked official image by digest, connects to its Postgres with TLS in verify-full mode against the site CA and does not turn on Keycloak's plain HTTP listener. Its Postgres runs as one replica with a certificate issued by site-pki, accepts connections only from the cluster's pod range, and its nightly dump also connects in verify-full mode.
statements.remarks: Your organization operates the site PKI that issues the database certificate.

implemented-requirements.description: Keycloak's data is kept on the encrypted site storage class.

statements.description: Keycloak's Postgres keeps its data volume and its nightly dumps on the site storage class, and every storage class the site stack renders is a Longhorn class with encryption on, keyed by the site's volume encryption key.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the volume encryption key's escrow copy.

implemented-requirements.description: The site runs a Keycloak release with the recorded flaw fixes.

statements.description: The site's signed evidence export reports the running Keycloak build and version, and the deployment collector passes it only for the upstream build at or above 26.8.0, the first upstream release that holds the fixes for CVE-2026-6856, as the dated record in the hosted verification records shows.
statements.remarks: Your organization upgrades the site's Keycloak from the signed offline bundle and produces the evidence export at least weekly.

control-implementations.description: Supply-chain statements generated from the component inventory. Do not edit by hand: run node compliance/src/cli.ts supply-chain-statements --write.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the component inventory lists its resources.

statements.description: The component inventory (compliance/resources.json) lists these resources for Site sign-in, each with the pin the repository uses: image quay.io/keycloak/keycloak 26.8.2@sha256:75b5c435a83b530caba5923922f93d47b2e3f8b4ad9e79200581122996653e55, image docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli 6.5.1-26.5.5@sha256:303b5c801fffbc34a8d47ff94bb7f00eba907418076a0061799424138ad16788, chart keycloakx 7.4.0 (sha256:9adcfc34dadced0c788e6cac0715bc9e9914c05304062e970fd6da3b8da46f1e) and tool postgresql 18.7 (sha256:67c997e865dee265d5194acafdd64db6a229cbb4bb56f5e6f0a67bc1572e0748). The compliance fit check over the whole repository, run as a CI test, fails when a resource the repository uses has no reviewed entry, or an entry lists a file that no longer uses it.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the inventory of what it installs at its site, with its owners, and reconciles it with this list.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the offline bundle import refuses a changed item.

statements.description: Before anything is copied to the site, the offline bundle import checks every item against the manifest your organization signed and refuses the bundle when an item is missing, extra or has another digest. For Site sign-in that covers image quay.io/keycloak/keycloak 26.8.2@sha256:75b5c435a83b530caba5923922f93d47b2e3f8b4ad9e79200581122996653e55, image docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli 6.5.1-26.5.5@sha256:303b5c801fffbc34a8d47ff94bb7f00eba907418076a0061799424138ad16788 and chart keycloakx 7.4.0 (sha256:9adcfc34dadced0c788e6cac0715bc9e9914c05304062e970fd6da3b8da46f1e). A CI test of the import proves the refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization builds and signs each bundle it approves with its own key, and imports only that bundle at its site.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: its resources are reviewed and pinned before use.

statements.description: These resources of Site sign-in each have a reviewed register entry with their licence, compliance fit and conditions, and are pinned as the component inventory lists them: image quay.io/keycloak/keycloak 26.8.2@sha256:75b5c435a83b530caba5923922f93d47b2e3f8b4ad9e79200581122996653e55, image docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli 6.5.1-26.5.5@sha256:303b5c801fffbc34a8d47ff94bb7f00eba907418076a0061799424138ad16788, chart keycloakx 7.4.0 (sha256:9adcfc34dadced0c788e6cac0715bc9e9914c05304062e970fd6da3b8da46f1e) and tool postgresql 18.7 (sha256:67c997e865dee265d5194acafdd64db6a229cbb4bb56f5e6f0a67bc1572e0748). The compliance fit check over the whole repository, run as a CI test, fails when one of them has no reviewed entry, is marked as not fitting, or is an image without a sha256 digest or an action without a full commit SHA.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects and accepts its suppliers and runs its own supply-chain risk management plan.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the offline bundle import accepts only what your organization signed.

statements.description: The offline bundle import accepts a bundle only when its manifest verifies with your organization's public key and refuses a bundle signed with any other key, so these items of Site sign-in reach the site only as your organization signed them: image quay.io/keycloak/keycloak 26.8.2@sha256:75b5c435a83b530caba5923922f93d47b2e3f8b4ad9e79200581122996653e55, image docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli 6.5.1-26.5.5@sha256:303b5c801fffbc34a8d47ff94bb7f00eba907418076a0061799424138ad16788 and chart keycloakx 7.4.0 (sha256:9adcfc34dadced0c788e6cac0715bc9e9914c05304062e970fd6da3b8da46f1e). A CI test of the import proves the refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the signing key, signs only the releases it approves, and keeps its own record of each bundle it imports.
